name_story.story: Tarik can be understood through the Arabic form طَارِق, whose central sense is tarik; one who knocks; night visitor. Tarik is Arabic طَارِق (Ṭāriq), the active participle of طَرَقَ, meaning 'one who knocks; night visitor'.

faq.a: Tarik is associated with the Arabic form طَارِق, whose core sense is tarik; one who knocks; night visitor.

faq.q: What is the origin of Tarik?
faq.a: Tarik is associated with Arabic. Tarik is Arabic طَارِق (Ṭāriq), the active participle of طَرَقَ, meaning 'one who knocks; night visitor'.
Yes — the underlying form طَارِق is Arabic.
Tarik can occur in Muslim naming contexts, but it is better described as a Arabic-origin name used within some Muslim naming traditions than as an exclusively Islamic religious term.
Tarik should not be classified as a Quranic personal name without a direct Quranic basis. The root ط ر ق is Quranic, but Ṭāriq is not itself a Quranic personal name.

faq.q: What does Tarik mean in Urdu?
faq.a: In Urdu, Tarik is rendered طارق and carries the sense طارق، رات کا آنے والا.

faq.q: What does Tarik mean in Persian?
faq.a: In Persian, Tarik is rendered طارق and carries the sense طارق، شب‌آیند.
A romanized syllable approximation is ta-rik. No IPA transcription is asserted because a verified phonetic transcription was not available.

faq.q: What are the variants of Tarik?
faq.a: Romanization variants include Tarik, tarik. Script forms are طارق, طَارِق, तारिक़.

faq.q: Is Tarik a boy's or girl's name?
faq.a: Documented usage records this form as male. Gender is not inferred from the meaning of the word, and actual use may vary between communities.
